Hi Kimberly — thanks again for the demo earlier today. High level notes from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can align with procurement and infra: 

- Current state: we run a mix of legacy GPU clusters (on-prem VMware) and some self-hosted model serving on bare-metal in our us-west datacenter.
- Preference: security team prefers a VPC/private deployment but finance is asking for a cost comparison that includes Dedicated capacity and staying with our self-hosted route.
- Migration concerns: how much work to port existing model artifacts and routing (we use an older HF transformer fork), and whether we can keep existing model weights on-prem while using Redwood for routing/traffic.

Questions we need answers to before the next internal steering meeting: 
1) Is a hybrid pattern supported — control plane in Redwood hosted but execution in our VPC (edge execution for PII-sensitive requests)?
2) Rough order of magnitude (per-inference) between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC for a mixed batch/low-latency workload (average 300 QPS peak, 20-token avg)?
3) What are the steps/estimate to migrate from our legacy GPU cluster to Redwood Private (on-prem bundle) — any pre-requisites or network requirements we should flag?

Also procuring SOC2 evidence and IP terms will be a procurement ask — can you attach the SOC2 checklist you mentioned?

Thanks — Alice
Alice Nolan
Head of ML Platform, Acme Health
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Hi Alice — great talking yesterday. Short answers up front and then a proposed next-step plan below. I’m attaching a one‑page MAP and our SOC2 evidence inventory (link + stub attached).

Quick answers:
- Hybrid control-plane with execution in customer VPC: supported via Redwood Private hybrid mode (control plane in hosted, execution nodes in customer VPC). We call this Hybrid VPC — useful for PII routing and data egress control.
- Cost buckets (very rough): Hosted API: lowest start-up cost, higher per-inference cost; Dedicated: lower per-inference at steady-state with reserved GPU pools; Private VPC/on‑prem: highest initial integration effort and infra cost but best for isolated data + predictable unit economics long-term. We’ll draft a simple cost model for your 300 QPS profile.
- Migration work: common path is (1) model compatibility check (weights + ops), (2) packaging container + small runtime shim, (3) KV cache/serving validation, (4) cutover and traffic ramp. For your legacy cluster we expect ~4–6 weeks of eng effort for a POC with one model, plus parallel run for validation.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll run a quick compatibility scan (we need one sample model artifact + sample traces).
2) Ben will draft an MoS (mutual action schedule) for migration and pricing options across the three modes.
3) Neha will surface SOC2 artifacts and an initial network checklist for on‑prem/VPC connectivity.

Action owners and timing: 
- Kimberly: coordinate PoC and stakeholder workshop (ETA: week of Oct 4)
- Ben: pricing + MoS (ETA: Oct 1)
- Neha: SOC2 evidence & network checklist (ETA: Oct 2)

I’ll attach the MAP and SOC2 inventory now. Let me know if you prefer a short workshop with your infra/security next Tuesday morning PDT.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Alice — looping in the pricing bits you asked for. Below are ballpark per-inference multipliers to use for internal decisioning (these are for illustration; we’ll produce a more exact cost model once we run the compatibility scan and confirm token distribution):

- Hosted API: baseline unit cost = 1.0x (no infra commit)
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): ~0.55–0.7x at 70%+ sustained utilization (savings scale with commit + term)
- Private VPC / On‑prem (managed by Redwood): ~0.6–0.8x after initial integration amortized (you carry infra + ops)

Notes: Dedicated gives you the most predictable per-token unit economics if you can commit. Private gives stronger isolation and may be preferred if your compliance team requires the control plane on-prem — but it pushes more of the ops burden to your side (or our on‑prem package).

I’ll include simple run-rate examples in the MoS: baseline monthly RPS, expected percent cached, reserved GPU size assumptions, and a 12/24-month term comparison.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
